posts.text:
Funding rates: the signal most crypto traders overlook entirely.

Quick primer on perpetual futures:

Perps have no expiry. To keep them anchored to spot price, exchanges use a funding mechanism — longs pay shorts (or vice versa) every 8h.

Why it matters:

→ Extremely positive funding = everyone is long, paying a premium. Liquidation cascade risk is real.

→ Extremely negative = shorts are paying. Squeeze risk.

→ Near zero = balanced. Trend-following works best.

Our Pump Radar checks funding across 200+ perpetual contracts daily. Extreme funding is one of the strongest contrarian signals we track.

→ tradingventureclub.com/results.html

What I'm watching this week, and why.

Bitcoin is in a confirmed downtrend on my screen: lower highs, lower lows, momentum pointing down.

The mistake most people make here is buying 'the dip' before the structure has changed. A dip in a downtrend is just a lower high waiting to happen. I don't look for longs until the market prints a higher low and holds it.

I spent ten years in business analysis before crypto. The habit that carried over: decide what would prove you wrong before you decide what you want to be true.

Mid-week read on Bitcoin, in plain language.

Everyone wants a direction call. Here's what the data actually says:

→ $BTC Fusion Score: 50/100 — not enough conviction either way
→ Smart Money verdict: neutral
→ Market regime: Trending Down

Nobody has an edge here, including the people who sound certain. A score in the middle means the layers disagree with each other, and when they disagree the market usually chops until one side gives up. My rule in this state: no new positions, smaller size if I'm already in, and I write down what would change my mind before it does.

I put these layers on one screen because I used to make the opposite mistake: trading the chart and finding out about the positioning afterwards.

What's your read on the current structure?

Price is a lagging indicator. By the time you see a breakout on the chart, the move has already been positioned for in derivatives.

Three derivatives signals I've found most predictive:

1. Open Interest divergence — OI surges but price stays flat = someone is building a massive position. Direction TBD, but volatility is coming.

2. Funding rate extremes — too crowded. The unwind becomes the trade.

3. Liquidation clusters — large clusters act like magnets. Market makers know where the stops are.

Our Pump Radar scans 200+ tokens every 5 minutes for exactly these patterns.

The edge isn't the data (it's public). The edge is systematizing the interpretation.
